correctness.rationale: For equal odd parity patterns, each coordinatewise minimum has that same parity, so the intersection is odd, giving at most 2^(n-1) elements. Binary prefix lifting gives an identity Gram matrix, hence the independent mn bound. Every pair in explicit 4-word and 8-word witnesses was directly recomputed; exhaustive clique checks gave exact 3/4-coordinate maxima across caps 1–3. At n=4 cap3, a complete exhaustive one-per-pattern DFS traverses 437 nodes and returns exactly six families, which are exactly the S4 orbit of the 8-word witness. Padding valid blocks by zeros and taking their union retains odd diagonal and even cross intersections, giving 8a+b_r for all a>=1 and r=0..3. Checks replay from the actual embedded program; the proof, not finite experiments, establishes all n.

value.rationale: The exact cap-three saturation of all odd parity patterns at n=3 and n=4 is the first sharp threshold contrasting the binary/cap-two regimes, and its n=4 extremizers have a complete six-family one-orbit classification. Direct sums give a uniform two-to-one asymptotic improvement O_3(n)>=2n-2 over the classical O_1(n)=n, while the standard oddtown embedding supplies O_3(n)<=3n. These results identify a motivated extremal phenomenon and a structural construction rather than a tiny isolated computation. The exact n>4 maximum is explicitly left open.
